author: Mark Atwood
text:
Filing 'human' because the bead presents two fix candidates without a recommendation and both are breaking changes (candidate 2 'add accessor methods' is also breaking — you cannot add inherent impl methods to a type alias in Rust, so any accessor-adding fix requires turning Invocation into a newtype struct first, breaking the 'inv.0/.1/.2' positional-access pattern).

Audit: 'Invocation' is used at 296 sites across the workspace. Every method handler in every server crate has the signature shape 'Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>'. Every client method-stub crate (mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata) constructs invocations via tuple literal '(method.to_owned(), args, CALL_ID.to_owned())'. Positional reads via 'inv.0/.1/.2' exist in base-client/src/client.rs:883 (matching call_id), wire-format docs, and tests. The cost of a struct-conversion is workspace-wide.

The workspace AGENTS.md does NOT have an explicit 'Invocation lock-in' policy paragraph the way it has 'Caller contract — wire-key collisions' for the extras pattern. This decision has not been explicitly deliberated.

Recommendation: keep the type alias (accept the lock); strengthen workspace AGENTS.md with a paragraph noting that 'pub type Invocation = (String, serde_json::Value, String)' is a deliberate forever-commitment that (a) pins consumers to serde_json's major version and (b) locks the 3-tuple positional-access shape for the lifetime of jmap-types ^0.1, citing the 296-site refactoring cost as the reason against revisiting.

Rationale for not autonomously applying the recommendation:
- The AGENTS.md edit codifies a workspace forever-commitment.
- The 296-site refactoring cost suggests the maintainer should explicitly ratify the lock rather than have it land via an api-contract bead close.
- Pre-0.2 is the cheapest time to revisit if maintainer wants candidate 1 (struct + serde_into/from).

Awaiting maintainer direction.
